results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Compared every independent outline summary with all 121 aligned controlling ideas, in order: 12 introduction units, 101 body units across 16 sections, and 8 conclusion units. Each has a substantive match to its aligned spec paragraph; the procedural questions, two implementation examples, economics synthesis, evaluation, stewardship and hand-off retain their declared functions. Broad summaries such as p101 still capture the paragraph's application of the hardware analogy to continuing human judgment. All 122 outline entries are retained with their exact summaries; the separately parsed opening callout maps to null because it is evidence attached to p001, not a separately specified paragraph. The supplied deterministic structure check independently reports matching sections, counts and forms.

Assessed all 105 prose units and 16 list units, including paragraphs that compare alternatives or define several terms serving one comparison. Each develops one controlling idea. The outliner's only two_ideas=true flag is Introduction callout: its summary correctly notices both inspectability and changed abstraction economics. This is the explicitly specified three-bullet KEY POINTS preview in p001 evidence, not one prose paragraph; the bullets preview related parts of the bounded thesis. Its flag was assessed rather than removed or silently treated as false, and its exact summary remains in the mapped outline.

Traced every one of the 121 aligned units through its explicit introduction/conclusion supports or its body section's supports. Review burden and changing platform knowledge serve S1; regular primitives and inspectable file operations serve S2; dependency expertise, wheel classification and ownership economics serve S3; frontend and messaging comparisons serve S4; specifications, tests, runtime visibility and review serve S5; shared rules, human responsibilities, risk controls and reflection serve S6. The introduction callout previews those claims. The conclusion combines them and its final boundary/hand-off extends S5/S6 without becoming an unrelated body argument. No orphan paragraph or unsupported section-level contribution was found.

Inspected all 71 declared evidence items (29 examples, 15 reasoning items, 6 sources, 6 quotations, 6 tables, 4 figures, 4 analogies and 1 scenario), plus their actual draft presentation. The platform comparison is interpreted by p031; the text-first table by p039; the three wheel classes by their Reason column and p053-p056; the economic questions by p080-p083; evaluation layers by their purpose column and p089-p090; and risk/control rows by their containment column, Figure 4 caption and p109-p112. All four figures have following captions stating their lesson. The three standalone blockquotes are followed by explanations or applied answers at p022, p047-p049 and p111. The opening callout, rejected frontend questions, and organization statement also have local argumentative context. The React, narrow dashboard, messaging, dependency and hardware examples are interpreted as bounded illustrations; none substitutes unexplained illustration for reasoning. Internal links have local explanations, and To Probe Further introduces no evidence required to follow the argument. This check assesses the draft's explanation of evidence, not external factual verification or the contents of image assets beyond their supplied alt text and captions.

Checked all 120 declared incoming boundaries: 103 paragraph transitions, 16 section transitions and the conclusion transition. Contrasts distinguish output from trust, fluid software from the hardware analogy, dependency benefits from costs, reuse from local generation, and simple platforms from missing safeguards. The cross-section prose explicitly moves from trust to the RISC test, shared understanding to file-based examples, visible files to imported behavior, frontend to messaging, both cases to economics, judgment to evaluation, evaluation to retained safeguards, criteria to team rules, and those rules to human stewardship and risks. The reflection questions operationalize that stewardship; the conclusion synthesizes it and makes the declared implementation-versus-model-product hand-off. The two local pauses reported by flow reader 1 concern immediate framing, not an absent or reversed declared relationship, and are recorded separately under flow_is_followable.

Compared paragraph openings and terms throughout all units and attachments with the inherited audience. RISC is expanded and explained before its software mapping; processor opcodes and the changing shared platform surface are described locally. Observability, blast radius, DOM, outbox/inbox, idempotency keys, contract tests, DRY, property/regression/golden tests, messaging failure vocabulary, mechanical sympathy, mutation/fault tests and blessed primitives receive explanations at their relevant first use. The earlier/later essay links supply local context rather than requiring the audience to know the journal's analogies. The closing contrast explains AI-assisted building versus a model inside the customer product. Named technologies in comparative inventories function as examples and do not require readers to know their internals to follow the claim. Neither flow reader reports an unexplained term, and no explicit does_not_know item needed for the argument remains unsupplied.

The introduction-only reader predicts the declared sequence: reviewer questions and complexity cost test; platform comparison and Claude Code/Codex; dependency risks and bounded reuse/generation criteria; simple-versus-primitive distinction; frontend and messaging cases; economic synthesis and evaluation; strategy, human ownership, risks and team questions. This covers all six roadmap promises and all 16 body sections in their planned order. The reader also correctly expects a bounded historical analogy, practical comparisons and illustrative cases rather than experiments or benchmarks, and an assertive but qualified practitioner tone. Its remaining uncertainty about the exact evaluation procedure is appropriate before reading the body.

The opening turns a concrete engineering concern about code volume into the harder trust question, supplies a local bridge from stable boundaries, and states a conditional thesis and detailed roadmap. It is not a generic placeholder or a restatement of an assigned question. The RISC definition and Patterson/Ditzel account serve an already established problem, so neither a dictionary opening nor a book-report pattern displaces the argument; there is no dawn-of-man preamble.

Final Thought brings together generation economics, continuing human capacity, stable boundaries, inspectable implementations, evaluation and ownership, then supplies a qualified course of action and explicit next-essay hand-off. It contains no in-conclusion opener, late unveiling of the thesis, sentimental appeal, unrelated evidence dump, or ending on a rephrased thesis alone. The final paragraph marks the scope boundary and names the next problem; it is the declared hand-off rather than a new supporting subargument smuggled into the conclusion. Some thesis restatement remains, as both flow readers observe, but it is accompanied by synthesis, consequence and action.

p116 combines stable boundaries from the opening with inspectable changes, specified behavior, evaluation and the human ability to maintain a growing system; no single body section states that whole connection. p115 explains why falling production cost leaves a trust cost, and p120 turns the combination into an action: select the smallest reliable platform, retain needed expertise, and verify output so cheaper generation becomes work the team understands and maintains. This realizes the conclusion's declared synthesis and its practical so-what, rather than only repeating the platform-size preference.

The opening contrasts how much code can be generated with how much of the generated system can be trusted. p115 returns explicitly to the diverging costs of producing and trusting code; p116 links generated structure to behavior users can rely on; and p120 explains how a reviewable, owned platform keeps more output from becoming an increasing review burden. These passages recover both elements named in conclusion.callback.to.

results.finding: Flow reader 1, paragraph on AI Changes the Economics of Abstraction, briefly checks whether this wording introduces a new decision framework, then recognizes a repetition and application of the earlier comparison. The section's declared role is synthesis, so calling the tradeoff new creates a small local expectation mismatch. Flow reader 2 explicitly experiences this section as synthesis rather than a change of subject; its general observation that the article repeats points does not corroborate this particular interruption.

AC-1 reader correctly expands Reduced Instruction Set Computer, identifies smaller regular building blocks and a qualified smallest-reliable-platform rule, and describes frameworks, libraries, packages, service APIs, conventions, tools and runtime behavior as the software instruction set. It explicitly includes both the producing agent and reviewing human and notes ongoing changes in versions, dependencies, APIs and local conventions. Its examples are explicit SQL, HTTP clients, local state and message handlers rather than the expected file/test/diff/version-control examples; these are accurate equivalent illustrations of the stated understanding outcome. The response satisfies the criterion without treating the hardware analogy as a literal recipe.

AC-2 reader permits the helper only when it is small, readable, tested, locally recoverable and owned, and rejects generation speed or shortness as proof of reliability. It preserves mature cryptography/authentication because specialist knowledge, edge cases, standards, safeguards and operating experience matter. It compares total review and maintenance burden and says a complex mature library can be the organization's simpler reliable choice. This meets every material distinction in the expected answer.

AC-3 reader supplies specifications; behavioral, edge-case, contract and failure-path tests including tests that catch broken behavior; logs and metrics for understanding and recovery; owners, shared primitives, current examples, dependency review and drift review. It identifies duplicated helpers, incompatible conventions, unsupported internal frameworks, missing safeguards, false confidence from short code, and complexity displaced into data assumptions, deployment, rollback, operations or maintenance. It retains mature expertise where the local alternative cannot replace it confidently. These satisfy the expected evaluation, stewardship and excessive-reduction outcomes.
